part: Running gear of the speedrun chassis: wheel suspension (front C-hubs with steering knuckles, rear hub carriers), axles with hex hubs, CVD drive shafts, steering (posts, bellcranks, links), servo with the floating servo mount, dampers and sway bars. Own design of the owner, partly based on the Carten T410R and deviating from it where the function requires; not verified. Files: cad/running_gear, generated with scripts/cad/generate_running_gear.py.
coordinate_system: Chassis plate coordinates (assembly): x across the car (+x right side seen toward End A), y along the car (End B at y = 0, End A front), z = 0 bottom face of the chassis plate. The parts of the right side are built and mirrored to the left side (x -> -x).

source_codes.manual: T410R instruction manual (design principle, sizes of screws, pins and bearings)
source_codes.derived: Calculated from other parts of the model
source_codes.design: Design choice for the function (own design, not measured)
source_codes.measured: Measured by the owner on the original part (caliper)

ride_height.note: Ride height front (End A) and rear (End B), setup sheet 4: axle heights 22.0 and 17.0 above the bottom face of the chassis plate.

wheel_centre_x.note: Wheel centre plane: overall width 190 over the tyres (30 mm wide), owner.

caster.note: Caster of the front kingpins (setup sheet 4), top toward the middle of the car.

kingpin_x.note: Front kingpin axis at the height of the axle; the centre of the outer CVD joint lies on it.

front_c_hub.note: Front C-hub: back plate from x to x, radius of the passage of the CVD drive shaft (owner: passage 10, the bone with its cross pin passes through), axial clearance to the knuckle at the top and the bottom (along the kingpin axis), height of the upper arm above its face toward the upper boss (flat top at z = axle height + 21.1 / 2 + 0.5 + 3.5 = 36.55), top of the back plate (seat of the camber ball stud, z). The back plate is closed (no slot, no pocket): the steering arm of the knuckle lies at the height of the axle and does not reach the back plate. The upper arm is solid from 1.0 above the ring of the knuckle up to its top, with a U-slot around the upper boss of the knuckle (0.5 clearance, open toward the wheel, so the knuckle slides in); only the boss turns in this space. Kingpin bores 5.0 for the guide sleeves (owner, see guide_sleeve). The caster of 10 degrees is in the C-hub: the kingpin bores and the faces toward the knuckle are square to the tilted kingpin axis, so the knuckle turns with a constant clearance.

front_c_hub_width.note: Width (y) of the C-hub: lower arm and back plate below z = 10.5 (between the rails of the wishbone, inner faces +-6.2), back plate above z = 10 (15: 2.5 wall beside the passage 10; free steering angle toward the middle 30 degrees, 37.5 with 13), upper arm (as wide as the back plate). The lug on the outer hinge pin is 13.0 long (outer gap of the wishbone 13.3).

knuckle.note: Front steering knuckle as the T410R knuckle (original part measured by the owner, measurement sheet K; manual step 15), built in the frame of the kingpin axis (origin in the centre of the outer CVD joint, x along the axle): bottom and top of the kingpin bosses along the kingpin axis (K8: 21.1 between the end faces, symmetric to the axle axis), radius of the bosses (K7: 7.0), radius of the ring (K1: 14.1), ring from x to x (K10: the inner end face lies on the kingpin axis; K2: 16.7 long), inner diameter of the lip between the bearings (K6: not measurable, the lip is approx. 1 high: 10 - 2 x 1), radius of the entry bore around the joint cup of the axle (K21: 12.4; the step to the bearing seat holds the end of the CVD drive shaft). 2 bearings 5x10x4 (manual) are pressed in from both ends against the lip (see knuckle_bores). The bosses sit on the kingpin axis above and below the inner end of the ring.

knuckle_bores.note: Bores of the knuckle: diameter of the bearing seats (K3: measured 9.98 on the original part, press fit of the bearings 10.0 within the accuracy of a caliper; the model uses the nominal 10.0 as the bearing seats of the bulkheads), length of each bearing seat from the end of the bore to the lip (K4: 4.29; the bearings rest on the lip, the outer bearing lies 0.29 below the end face), length of the entry bore from the inner end face (K21: 5.79, section of the joint cup of the axle; the joint cup reaches up to 0.2 before the step, a shoulder 6.5 rests on the inner race of the inner bearing), diameter of the kingpin bores in the bosses (K9: 2.7, depth 4.5 from the end face of the boss; the bores end at the entry bore). The lip is the rest (K5, not measurable, calculated by the owner): 16.7 - 5.79 - 2 x 4.29 = 2.33. Kingpins: set screws M3x8 threaded into the bores 2.7 (thread formed by the screw, 4.3 long in the boss); they turn with the knuckle in the bores 3.1 of the C-hub. The top set screw is inserted from above through the upper arm of the C-hub, the bottom set screw from below before the outer hinge pin.

guide_sleeve.note: Guide sleeves of the kingpins in the bores 5.0 of the C-hub (owner: bores 5.0, sleeves just under 5.0 so that they fit without pressing; manual step 15: flanged sleeves): outer diameter, inner diameter (the screw M3 passes), flange diameter and thickness (manual drawing scaled to the outer diameter), wall between the lower bore and the outer hinge pin. Top: flanged sleeve from above on a spot face square to the kingpin axis, the shank reaches the end face of the upper boss; the screw M3x8 clamps it to the knuckle, so knuckle, sleeve and screw turn together in the bore of the C-hub (as the original). Bottom (deviation from the original, the outer hinge pin lies only 2.4 beside the kingpin axis): plain sleeve in a bore that ends above the outer hinge pin, 0.4 above the lower face of the C-hub (thrust face, 0.1 play to the boss); set screw M3x8 from below through a hole 3.1, inserted before the outer hinge pin.

steering_arm_ball.note: Steering arm of the knuckle as the T410R knuckle (measured by the owner): x of the ball stud (outer hole; K12/K13: from the kingpin axis 5.0 toward the chassis, then 25.0 square to it toward the middle of the car), y relative to the kingpin axis, thickness of the flat arm (along the kingpin axis; K15: 4.9 at the end tab), thickness of the gussets at the bosses (K16, not measured), distance of the second hole toward the ring (K14, not measured), height of the middle plane of the arm above the axle axis (K17: 0, in the middle, owner), width of the end tab (K18: 7.4). The arm has a wide root along the ring, runs diagonally inboard and ends in a tab straight back with the 2 holes. Ball stud on top of the arm (as the original); the steering link rises from the bellcrank ball (18.75) to the knuckle ball (24.0 above the bottom face of the chassis plate). With the bellcranks of this model the original ball position gives Ackermann 102 / 115 / 130 % at 15 / 20 / 25 degrees of the inner wheel.

rear_carrier.note: Rear hub carrier as the original part (photos of the owner), in the frame of the rear arm (x along the arm from the outer hinge pin): length of the tube (bearing housing, owner: 10; its outer end is flush with the lug on the outer hinge pin), outer diameter of the tube (photo, scaled with the bearing seat 10: approx. 14.6), width of the web on the inner end of the tube (design), top (z, seat of the camber stud). Lower lug between 2 spacers 3x7x3 on the outer hinge pin. The 2 bearings 5x10x4 sit in the ends of the tube against a lip of 2.0. A sloped arm runs from the inner end of the tube up to the seat of the camber stud (photo); the position of the camber ball comes from the camber link. The original part has 2 holes in the top tab (positions of the camber stud, photo); the model has the one at the position of the camber link.

axle.note: Axles: diameter in the bearings 5x10x4 (manual), thread M4 at the end for the wheel nut, outer diameter (owner: 10) and length of the joint cup.

hex_hub.note: Hex hubs 12 mm (spec_tires.yaml), width front and rear (manual: 6 and 7 mm; the rear gains 2 mm of track, as on the car of the owner), pin 2x10 through the axle in a slot of the hub, grub screw M3x3.

cvd.note: CVD drive shafts: bone diameter, end balls, cross pins 2x8 in the slots of the outdrive cups and of the joint cups of the axles.

post.note: Steering posts on H24/H25 (owner): hexagon 5.5 across the flats, height of the hexagon, journal 5.0 for 2 bearings 5x8x2.5; thread M3 at both ends (screw from below through the chassis plate, screw with washer on top).

bellcrank.note: Bellcranks as the T410R (manual steps 13 and 14): straight levers on the posts; bottom and top (z), length of the ball arm (forward, toward End A), offset of its ball toward the middle of the car (-1.0: ball at x = +-20.7, on the line of the inner hinge pins against bump steer), length of the rear arm to the bridge. The ball arm moves the ball of the steering link across the car. Ball stud on top (thread M3), bearings 5x8x2.5 on the posts.

bridge.note: Rigid steering bridge as the T410R (manual step 13): bottom (z: 1.0 above the centre driveshaft), thickness, width, depth of the boss behind the bridge with the thread M3 for the ball stud of the servo link (stud toward End B). The bridge joins the rear arms of the bellcranks behind the posts and moves across the car; it turns on 2 spacers (collar 7.0 from the bellcrank to the bridge, sleeve 5.0 in the bridge), screws M3x18 into the bellcranks.

servo.note: Servo (spec_servo.yaml, low profile): length, width, height incl. output spline. Mounted as the T410R (manual step 10): across the car, output shaft and horn facing forward (End A), output at the outer end of the case; the case starts at x = 12.5 (beside the centre driveshaft). The servo hangs on the floating servo mount (see servo_mount); its height is kept from the previous mount (4.5 above the chassis plate), so the steering is unchanged.

servo_mount.note: Floating servo mount as the T410R (manual step 10, photos of the owner): a top plate above the servo on 2 posts; only the fixed post at the inner end of the servo is screwed onto the chassis plate (H17/H21, owner, threads M3 from below), the floating post at the output end hangs from the top plate and ends at the bottom of the servo (4.5 above the chassis plate). The servo ears are screwed to the front faces of the posts (threads M3 from the front), the top plate to the top faces (threads M3 from above, slots at the floating post for other servo lengths). Values (design): thickness of the top plate, gap between the servo and the top plate, width of the posts (x), material around the screws H17/H21 along y (the fixed post reaches with a foot below the inner servo ear to H21), depth of the leg of the floating post (y), thickness and length of its top flange, width and depth of the U-notch from the top of the fixed post (as the T410R), front edge of the top plate behind the front face of the servo case (the servo sits nearly flush with the front end of the mount, owner and photos). Servo Savox SC-1252MG+ 40.8 x 20.2 x 25.4 (spec_servo.yaml); the position of the ears (flange 7.5 behind the front face of the case) is not taken from a drawing of the manufacturer.

servo_horn.note: Clamp servo horn (aluminium, 25T, no servo saver: spec_servo.yaml): length to the ball stud (vertical in the centre position, manual step 10), width, thickness. The ball moves across the car and pushes the bridge through the servo link (gap 21, manual: B).

damper.note: Standard 1:10 on-road damper: body diameter, cap diameter, spring diameter, shaft diameter, body length, spring wire.

sway_bar.note: Sway bars as the T410R (manual step 23, photos of the owner): wire 1.4, height of the bar in the holders (z), position of the holders outside the screw holes of the tabs of the lower bulkhead (y in the coordinates of the bulkhead), half length of the straight part in the holders (screws M3x6 from above into the tabs). The bar is a plain trapezoid (manual step 23): from the straight part a straight leg runs on each side to the ball end above the ball stud of the arm (no bend at the end).

sway_link.note: Drop links of the sway bars (manual step 22): 2 rod ends on a set screw M3x12 with a gap of 3.0 between the rod ends. Rod ends as the camber links (9.0 from the ball centre to the face, assumed): 21.0 between the ball centres. The link stands vertical between the ball stud in rail B of the arm (inner hole) and the ball end of the bar.

sway_ball_end.note: Ball end on each end of the sway bar (aluminium, manual step 23 and photos of the owner): ball for the rod end of the drop link, neck diameter, collar diameter and length, start of the collar from the ball centre. Bore for the bar along the axis up to the ball centre; grub screw M3x3 from the top into the collar (manual step 23). The ball end sits on the axis of the leg.

ball_offset.note: Ball studs: centre of the ball 4.0 from the face of the part (neck 3.0, thread M3 into the part).

damper_plane.note: Dampers in the plane 8.3 in front of the damper face of the shock towers (spring collar 15.0 plus 0.8); the lower ball stud along the hole of the shock plate reaches this plane.

steering_lock.note: Required steering angle of the front knuckles in both directions; the generator reports the free angle (no contact of the knuckle, the axle and the steering arm with the C-hub, the CVD drive shaft and the wishbone).
